speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing headaches and worsening vision for three weeks. To help me understand your condition, have your headaches been constant or do they come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the progressive nature of your symptoms, have you noticed any specific changes in your vision, such as blurriness, double vision, or a dark spot obscuring part of your view?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Brain Tumor (Glioblastoma or Metastasis).

The clinical picture of a new, progressive headache and worsening vision in a 69-year-old is highly concerning for an intracranial mass lesion causing increased intracranial pressure and compressive optic neuropathy. Given your urgency, I am requesting immediate imaging to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
